national_news.title: PM Narendra Modi Holds 15 Bilateral Meetings on Sidelines of BRICS Summit
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi conducted 15 bilateral meetings with heads of state and government on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
Held talks with leaders from Kazakhstan, Egypt, Indonesia, Philippines, South Africa, Nigeria, China, Russia, Iran, and UN Secretary-General.
During discussions, the Philippines formally decided to join the India-led Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI).

national_news.title: Amit Shah Addresses 52nd Gems & Jewellery Awards, Urges Boost in Lab-Grown Diamonds
bullets: Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressed the 52nd India Gems and Jewellery Awards ceremony in Mumbai, emphasizing lab-grown diamonds as a major opportunity.
Stated that the lab-grown diamond market volume is projected to grow nearly 50 times, calling for end-to-end domestic ecosystem capabilities.
Inaugurated a manuscript exhibition titled 'Shri Ganesh Dnyanarati' at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai to promote manuscript preservation through digital technology.

national_news.title: Mizoram's 51.38-km Bairabi-Sairang Rail Line Completes One Year of Operations
bullets: The 51.38-km Bairabi-Sairang railway line in Mizoram completed one year of operation, serving over 15 lakh passengers and delivering 2,500+ freight wagons.
The rail line features 153 bridges and 45 tunnels spanning 16 km, with its tallest bridge measuring 114 metres in height.
Direct train connectivity to Delhi, Kolkata, Guwahati, and Silchar led to an 86% increase in tourism across Mizoram during its inaugural year.

national_news.title: Bairabi-Sairang Railway Project Transforms Mobility and Freight Access in Mizoram
bullets: Ministry of Railways marked one year of the Bairabi-Sairang line, inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on September 13, 2025, extending rail connectivity near capital Aizawl.
The line incorporates 4 new stations—Hortoki, Kawnpui, Mualkhang, and Sairang—and features a 114-meter-tall bridge, 42 meters taller than the Qutub Minar.
Operationalized key long-distance services including the Sairang-Anand Vihar Rajdhani Express and Silchar passenger train, enhancing connectivity with Assam's Barak Valley.

national_news.title: Rashtriya Raksha University Concludes BRICS AML/CFT Capacity Building Programme
bullets: Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU) hosted the valedictory ceremony for a five-day BRICS Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) training programme.
The international capacity-building initiative focused on emerging risks, FATF methodologies, and strengthening cross-border financial security and compliance frameworks.
The event highlighted India’s robust AML/CFT ecosystem and high technical compliance recognized in the 2024 FATF Mutual Evaluation.

national_news.title: Prime Minister Chairs BRICS Session on Inclusive Global Governance in New Delhi
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the BRICS session on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism” during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
The Prime Minister emphasized transforming the 'pyramid of privilege' into a 'platform of partnership' to give the Global South greater representation in bodies like the UN Security Council.
Key proposals included the establishment of a Seafarers Emergency Support Network and adopting the New Delhi BRICS Leaders' Declaration.

national_news.title: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Expands Welfare Measures for Senior Citizens
bullets: Over 2.88 lakh senior citizens have benefited from essential care, support services, shelter, and healthcare facilities under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
The government sanctioned 142 new Senior Citizen Homes across the country to expand institutional care infrastructure.
Around 23.93 lakh free assistive living devices (wheelchairs, hearing aids, walking sticks) were distributed across 228 camps for eligible BPL beneficiaries.

national_news.title: India Poutlines Key BRICS Initiatives at 18th Summit
bullets: India's BRICS Sherpa Sudhakar Dalela briefed media on key initiatives proposed during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
Proposals included the BRICS Troika mechanism to ensure continuity between outgoing, current, and incoming chairs.
India pushed for a roadmap for reforming global governance structures and assistance measures for stranded seafarers and the Global South.

national_news.title: BRICS Summit 2026 Features Dravidian Architecture at Bharat Mandapam
bullets: The 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi showcased South India's architectural heritage with a grand corridor replicating the Rameswaram temple at Bharat Mandapam.
The corridor design was inspired by Tamil Nadu’s Ramanathaswamy Temple, a prominent site in the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit built in the Dravidian style.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi utilized this architectural display to showcase India's regional heritage to leaders from all eleven BRICS member nations.

national_news.title: BRICS Leaders Adopt New Delhi Declaration and Condemn Pahalgam Terror Attack
bullets: BRICS leaders unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration on the opening day of the BRICS Summit hosted under India's chairship.
The bloc condemned the April 2025 terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, reaffirming a policy of zero tolerance for terrorism in all forms.
The declaration urged member nations to act against cross-border movement of terrorists, terror financing, safe havens, and UN-designated terrorist entities.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Chief Minister Urges Assistant Professors to Ensure 75% Student Attendance
bullets: Bihar Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary addressed newly appointed assistant professors, urging them to ensure at least 75% student attendance in degree colleges.
The state government recently established 211 new degree colleges and appointed 2,451 assistant professors to expand higher education infrastructure, particularly in rural areas.
Highlighted that Bihar spends over 21% of its total state budget on the education sector, spanning primary, secondary, and higher education.

bihar_news.title: Bihar to Send 100 Professors to Oxford and Global Institutions for Training
bullets: Bihar government announced a plan to select 100 college professors and send them for 1-month training programs at Oxford and other reputed global universities.
The initiative aims to expose state educators to international teaching standards and facilitate experience-sharing with global academic experts.
The initiative was unveiled during the orientation program for 2,451 assistant professors recruited across 211 newly created degree colleges in the state.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Launches Key Initiatives in Higher Education and Model Schools
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister inaugurated an orientation programme for 2,451 newly appointed assistant professors across 211 newly created degree colleges, making Bihar the first state to launch 211 degree colleges in a single day.
The state announced the development of 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan model schools to provide quality education along with NEET/JEE coaching, live classes, and 24x7 online tutoring.
An initiative was announced to send 100 selected professors for training to top global institutions including Oxford University, backed by an allocation of 21% of the state budget to education.

bihar_news.title: Bihar CM Launches Model School Development & Educator Training Programs
bullets: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary inaugurated an orientation program for 2,451 newly appointed assistant professors across 211 degree colleges at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna.
Announced the development of 700 Saraswati Vidya Niketan model schools offering NEET and JEE competitive exam coaching, live classes, and 24x7 online tutoring.
Reiterated plans to send 100 professors to Oxford University for global exposure and professional training, supported by 21% state budget allocation for the education sector.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Sets 75% Attendance Goal and Plans Global Exposure for College Faculty
bullets: The Bihar government has established 211 new degree colleges and appointed 2,451 assistant professors to expand higher education infrastructure, especially in rural areas.
The state government announced plans to identify 100 college teachers to send abroad for one-month training courses at top international institutions.
Bihar currently allocates over 21% of its annual state budget towards the education sector, spanning primary schools to higher education institutions.
